founder_profile.idea: Dog walking service in my neighborhood
founder_profile.experience: Grew up with dogs, no business experience

market.summary: Busy working owners and older residents are the most likely customers. A 30-minute walk at $20 is a fair starting price for a local, reliable walker.
key_findings: Best customers: busy working pet owners and older residents
Regular weekday walks are steadier income than one-off visits
Trust is the main selling point: reviews and a clean background check help
Neighborhood apps and vet office bulletin boards reach owners cheaply
assumptions: Assumes about 3 walks a week per regular customer

risks.risk: Big app-based walking services compete on convenience

next_steps: Offer a free first walk to 5 neighbors
Ask your first customers for written reviews

legal.summary: Dog walking has few licensing steps, but liability insurance matters because you are responsible for someone else's pet.
key_findings: Sole proprietor is the simplest way to start
Get a free EIN (tax ID) from the IRS
Check whether your city requires a general business license
Use a simple written agreement with each client
assumptions: Fees are estimates; confirm with your city and county

risks.risk: Without insurance, an injury or lost dog could cost far more than the business earns

needs_from_others.request: Include pet-care liability insurance in monthly costs

next_steps: Get quotes for pet-care liability insurance

finance_raw.summary: Dog walking is cheap to start. Your main ongoing cost is insurance.
key_findings: Insurance is the biggest monthly bill
Almost all of each walk's price is yours to keep
assumptions: Insurance price is a typical estimate; get real quotes
next_steps: Set up a free scheduling and payment app

responses_to_others.request: Include pet-care liability insurance in monthly costs
responses_to_others.answer: Included: about $45 a month for pet-care liability insurance.

roadmap.one_sentence: Reliable, local dog walks for busy owners in Milledgeville.
roadmap.verdict_title: Ready to launch, with one heads-up
roadmap.verdict_text: Low costs and steady demand make this a strong first business. Watch your hours before you take on too many clients.

watch_out.title: Watch your hours
watch_out.text: Scout expects about 180 walks a month. At 30 minutes each plus travel, that may be more than 15 hours a week.
watch_out.how_found: Ward compared Scout's demand with your hours, Scout suggested group walks, and Penny re-checked the numbers.

watch_out.title: Get insured before your first walk
watch_out.text: Quill flagged liability insurance as the most important step, since you are responsible for someone else's pet.

first_steps: Offer a free first walk to 5 neighbors
Set up a scheduling and payment app
Ask your first clients for reviews
roadmap.go_verdict: This is one of the easiest businesses to start. Get insured, start with a few neighbors, and use group walks so your hours go further.
